newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares close mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares close mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Stocks at major Indian exchanges ended little changed amid sluggish trade on Tuesday, with price movements limited by a lack of market-moving news, dealers said.
"The market is slightly stagnant. People are looking for a correction," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Securities.
The Bombay index has reacted 265 points, or about seven percent from this month's high of 4,029 due to profit-taking.
The Industry Ministry, in a statement on Tuesday said India's 24-sector industrial production index rose by five percent in January over the same month in 1996.
"The market has already sent the first correction after the post-budget optimism," said Sachin Joneja, research head at Classic Share & Stock Brokers.

Bombay shares rocketed 16 percent after the government last month presented a market-friendly 1997/98 (April-March) budget, but fell back later on profit-taking. A period of consolidation will pave the way to sustaining the rally, dealers said.

"It is now sinking in that the impact of the budget will take some time to be felt on corporate bottomlines. Foreign institutional investors are not going to come rushing in to buy Indian stocks," said Classic's Joneja.
"There is hardly any action. Buyers are staying on the sidelines," said a local trader.
Tuesday is the last day of the weekly account at the NSE and activity was mostly business-squaring deals, he said.
Shares of SmithKline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd jumped 26.75 rupees or 9.9 percent, to 296.75 at the Bombay exchange on news the firm was meeting to decide on a bonus equity issue.
The company, in a statement released after the close of trade, said it had decided to offer shareholders a bonus issue of three shares for every five shares held.
